To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of the video stream is affected by the codec and the packetization method.

the quality of the video is dependent upon the packetization of the video stream, the codec used, the bitrates used and the packet error characteristics; the impact of packet errors on the video stream depends on the packetization and codec used, and that the impact is different for CBR and VBR streams, as well as for different codecs.

for the VBR case, the video quality is determined by: (1) the codec used; (2) the packet size; (3) the number of packets per Group Of Pictures (GOP); and, (4) the packet loss rate; while for the CBR case the video quality is primarily determined by the packet size and the packet loss rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of network errors on video quality, and how this can vary with the spatial dimension, the codec, and the bitrate.
the impact of packetization and packet loss visibility on video quality, and how this varies with the spatial and temporal resolution of the video stream, and whether the codec used is H.264 or HEVC.
the visibility of packet loss in video; and, how to assess the impact on quality, for different resolutions and codecs.

(i) the packet loss visibility is a strong function of the spatial resolution; (ii) the packet loss sensitivity is also a function of the spatial resolutions and the codec, and is more sensitive for the HEVC codec; (iii) packet loss is more visible for the VBR than the CBR, with the latter more sensitive to the codec; and (iv) packet loss visibility is not a function of the codec, but is a function of the packet reordering and the duplication.
the impact of packet retransmission is not as significant as that of packet loss, and that the impact of reordering and duplication can be significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with the current generation of codecs, the impact of packet loss on quality is relatively low.
, for VBR streams, packet loss is not a major factor in determining the quality of the displayed stream.
the impact of packet loss and re-ordering on the video quality is dependent on the codec used and the spatial resolution, with HEVC showing a greater resilience to packet loss than H.264.
